title: Work and energy transfer mark scheme

option_feedback.A: 30 N is the vertical component, 50 sin 37 degrees, rather than the horizontal component.
option_feedback.B: Correct. The horizontal component is 50 cos 37 degrees = 39.9 N, which rounds to 40 N.
option_feedback.C: 50 N is the original force magnitude, not its horizontal component.
option_feedback.D: 63 N comes from dividing by cos 37 degrees, which would make a component larger than the original force.

marking_points.text: Selects B, corresponding to 50 cos 37 degrees = 40 N for the horizontal component.

questions.answer: Work done is the product of force and displacement in the direction of the force.
accepted_alternatives: force multiplied by distance moved in the direction of the force

marking_points.text: States that work done is the product of force and displacement in the direction of the force.

option_feedback.A: Negative work would require a force component opposite to the displacement. The support force is perpendicular to it.
option_feedback.B: Correct. The upward force has zero component along the horizontal displacement, so its work is zero.
option_feedback.C: 45 is the force magnitude in newtons, not a work value in joules.
option_feedback.D: 45 × 8.0 ignores that force and displacement are perpendicular.

marking_points.text: Selects B, recognising that the upward support force does zero work during horizontal displacement.

option_feedback.A: 19 J results from dividing distance by force and does not use the component along displacement.
option_feedback.C: 260 J uses the perpendicular component 75 sin 60 degrees instead of the parallel component.
option_feedback.D: 300 J uses the full 75 N although the force is not parallel to displacement.

marking_points.text: Selects B, corresponding to (75 cos 60 degrees) × 4.0 = 150 J.
